thread:
emma: Hey, incoming escalation from Jake (enterprise customer). They're seeing intermittent 429s and requests routed to the shared fallback pool instead of their Dedicated pool. Started ~08:15 UTC.

jake-customer: we started seeing spikes at 08:14, latency jumps to 2s and then 429s. Everything worked before last deploy. No changes on our side.

emma: Can you paste a quick repro curl that hits the Dedicated endpoint? Also which tenant header are you sending?

jake-customer: curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX' -H 'X-Redwood-Tenant: acct-tenant-123' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

emma: thanks. Raj, Lina — can you check routing logs for tenant acct-tenant-123 around 2056789000? Looks like control plane might have returned a fallback pool id.

raj: looking. I see a burst of route-decisions where the tenant header is missing on the controlplane side for ~20 requests. Those requests matched the 'default' pool selector and went to shared. Sample controlplane log: 
```
2026-03-17T08:14:32Z INFO route_decision tenant="" selector="default" pool_id="shared-cold-01" request_id=rx1a2b3
```

lina: interesting — envoy sidecar telemetry shows header rewrite on the sidecar proxy for some requests: 'x-tenant' -> 'x-redwood-tenant' normalization ran, but in a couple traces the header was dropped when the auth sidecar rewrote Authorization and re-serialized headers.

tina: that would cause the control plane to not see tenant, so routing falls through. Any config changes in the last deploy to sidecar header handling?

emma: There was a small deploy last night touching the auth sidecar image (token introspection + header canonicalization). Rolling back to previous image seems to stop reproducing for Jake (can we confirm).

raj: I pulled request traces. Repro steps:
1) Send request with both Authorization and X-Redwood-Tenant header.
2) auth-sidecar performs introspection, then calls header-normalizer.
3) header-normalizer uses header map -> iterates keys, lowercases, then appends canonical names. There's an edge-case when header keys are mutated during iteration resulting in skip of certain keys. Code snippet: 
```
for k := range hdr {
  nk := strings.ToLower(k)
  hdr[nk] = hdr[k]
  delete(hdr, k)
}
```
This can lose headers if delete happens before read of the next key.

lina: nice catch. That explains intermittent nature (depends on map iteration order). Impact: tenant header occasionally lost -> control plane fallback -> requests to shared pool -> throttles for customer.

emma: Severity: high for Dedicated customers. Action items: 1) Hotfix sidecar to use a new map build (create new map then replace) and release ASAP. 2) Backfill affected requests and credit the tenant for throttled tokens. 3) Add e2e test to catch header-preservation in auth+normalizer chain. 4) Add route-decision invariant logging when a tenant header is absent and request is for a Dedicated plan.

tina: I'll coordinate hotfix rollout. Plan: cut 2056789-hotfix branch, build image, run canary in staging, then quick rollback path. ETA 2 hours.

raj: I added a temp guard in controlplane: if tenant header empty but Authorization token decodes to a known tenant, use token-subject to route (best-effort) — toggled off by default but can be enabled for affected customers. Should we enable for Jake while fix rolls out?

emma: yes enable for acct-tenant-123 only. Jake please confirm whether you want the temporary mitigation.

jake-customer: please enable mitigation, we have production traffic. Credits appreciated.

lina: also adding unit/regression test now. Pushing patch: commit 9f3b2c. Patch uses new map copy pattern and preserves header order.

ops-bot: deploy triggered by tina: container=auth-sidecar:v2056789-hotfix -> staging canary (2 pods)

tina: Canary looks good after 15 minutes (no header drops in 10k requests). Promoting to prod in 10. I'll post rollback window.

emma: QA: validate route_decision logs for acct-tenant-123 show pool_id = dedicated-acct-tenant-123 after rollout. Also verify no 429s in last 30m.

raj: enabled controlplane token-fallback for acct-tenant-123. Monitoring on.

ops-bot: deploy promoted to prod: auth-sidecar:v2056789-hotfix by tina at 08:43 UTC

jake-customer: Confirmed — routing fixed, latency back to normal, no 429s. Thanks.

emma: follow-ups: (1) postmortem with root cause (header mutation during map iteration) and remediation (patch, tests, enable code review checklist), (2) customer credits and short incident summary to Jake, (3) add a lint/test to sidecar repo to detect in-place map mutations on header transforms.

lina: I'll draft a short postmortem and assign owners.

emma: Great. Marking incident resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
